question: Which Foundation (根器) does the player unlock upon clearing Chapter 4? 1. Envious Tongue (舌尝思) 2. Fuming Ears (耳听怒) 3. Hubris Nose (鼻嗅爱) 4. Craving Eyes (眼看喜) 5. Grieved Body (身本忧)

rollouts.answer: 3. Hubris nose (鼻嗅爱), citing a screen at ~44,330-44,368s

agent tries to re-fetch the full text of row episodes:30sec:002103 with a json_extract() SQL call that assumes JSON-wrapped text; the 30sec-granularity column is a plain string here, so the query errors out and the lead is dropped instead of being retried with a plain SELECT.

clip_qa is instead pointed at 44310-44430s, a screen that is actually the Chapter 3 reward (occurs before the Chapter 4 title card at 44550-44610), and correctly reads on-screen text '鼻嗅爱' there; the agent treats this as the Chapter-4 unlock.

the agent discards this correct visual answer and instead submits 'Hubris nose', reasoning from an unrelated ordinal scheme built on two chapter-transition timestamps (44,550s and 76,830s) that places nose 'between the earlier tongue foundation and the later body foundation' -- a chain of reasoning not grounded in anything actually retrieved.

db_evidence.notes: episodes:30sec:002103 / visual_clips:002103 (63090-63120s), squarely inside a run_sql BETWEEN 62500/62800-63400/63600 sweep over the clue interval, textually describes the post-chapter-4 根器 menu cycling through ear ('耳听风吟'), nose ('鼻嗅变'), then tongue ('舌尝识'). Frames pulled directly at 63096s (nose, no highlight) and 63110s (tongue, with a bright glow/highlight around the selected icon) corroborate that tongue is the newly-selected/unlocked foundation, matching reference answer '1'. A confusable distractor exists at 44310-44430s (before the Chapter 4 title card at 44550-44610s): this is the Chapter 3 reward screen and genuinely displays '鼻嗅爱' (Hubris Nose) as an already-unlocked companion/根器 entry, unrelated to the Chapter 4 question; this appears to be the source of the 'Hubris nose' answer's plausibility.

root_causes: Confusable distractor in the memory DB: a genuine on-screen '鼻嗅爱' (Hubris Nose) 根器 screen exists just before the Chapter 4 title card (44310-44430s, actually Chapter 3's own reward), and two rollouts (0, and implicitly the training data behind rollout 1/2's prior) anchored on this earlier, unrelated screen or its answer instead of the true post-chapter-4 clue window.

Under-sampling by the visual sub-agent: clip_qa in rollout 2 sampled only 2 frames near the start of a 150s window where the 根器 selection cycles through 3 entries, catching the mid-cycle 'nose' item rather than continuing to the highlighted 'tongue' item that appears ~15-20s later.

Answer-stage override of correct evidence: rollout 3's clip_qa correctly identified 'envious tongue' with a highlighted unlock effect, but the final submit_answer discarded this and substituted an unsupported ordinal/positional argument based on unrelated chapter-transition timestamps.

A one-off SQL execution error (json_extract on a plain-string column) in rollout 0 caused the agent to abandon a promising already-in-range lead (episodes:30sec:002103) rather than retry with a plain SELECT, redirecting it to the wrong time window.
Rollout 1 retrieved the exact correct text passage (ear->nose->tongue cycling) but simply picked the wrong (middle) item as the answer -- a plain misread with no other explanatory tool-call anomaly.
what_worked: Rollout 4 ran a single well-targeted run_sql over the 30sec-granularity episodes table spanning the clue interval, and read the resulting cycling-menu description correctly without needing any visual verification.
When clip_qa was aimed precisely at the clue window and sampled frames late enough in it (rollout 3, 63115-63116s), it correctly identified the tongue foundation with its unlock highlight.
transferable_lessons: For 'reward/unlock right after chapter N' questions, first locate the chapter-N-completion title card/boss-defeat event via SQL/semantic search, then only look at 根器/menu evidence strictly AFTER that timestamp; screens shown before the chapter's own title card belong to the previous chapter's reward, not the current one, even if they show a plausible option from the answer list.

When a UI element (e.g. a scrollable wheel of items) is being cycled through in a video, sample multiple frames across the full described interval (not just the first couple of seconds) to find the terminal/highlighted item, since only the newly-unlocked entry (not every entry shown) answers 'which one was just unlocked'.

Trust visual sub-agent (clip_qa) evidence that has a specific, cited, unlock-state detail (glow/highlight, '悟'/confirm prompt) over post-hoc ordinal reasoning built from unrelated timestamps; do not let the final answer step override a directly-verified visual read with an unverified inference chain.

When a SQL call errors (e.g. json_extract on a non-JSON column), retry with a corrected query on the same row rather than abandoning that lead and searching elsewhere, especially if the row was already flagged as containing the target keyword/topic.
open_questions: Whether the '悟'/highlight visual cue that rollout 3's clip_qa cited at 63115-63116s is reliably distinguishable from ordinary cursor-hover styling by a human reviewer without game domain knowledge, versus being an artifact of the sub-agent's own confidence.

Whether the Chapter 3 vs Chapter 4 title-card boundary (44550-44610s vs 62820-62850s) is unambiguous enough in the DB for a rollout that never queries semantic_triples/event_steps for chapter-title markers to reliably avoid the Chapter-3 nose distractor.
